title: fix(update): recover when the package publication journal no longer matches the installation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #186314. A manual npm install or copied installation after an interrupted update can leave a package publication journal that blocks every later CLI or Control UI update with `update-recovery-pending`.

## User Impact

The next update can retire obsolete recovery custody with a warning and continue. The current package and launchers remain untouched, and the journal, helper, and retained package trees are preserved for diagnostics. No schema, dependency, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Package activation settlement already owns recovery admission. It now recognizes an external installation only when neither recorded package generation nor any recorded published launcher remains installed. Inode comparisons exclude the old generations even across a remount. Changed journal bindings permit settlement only; they never grant publication or restoration authority. Live executor authority and the replacement observation are checked again before settlement. Dry-run uses the same eligibility decision without changing state.

Still-installed candidates continue through verification and settlement; incomplete publication and live launcher custody still require recovery. The existing selected-Node compatibility check already runs before journal creation. Coverage now includes the reported Node 26.4.0 runtime.

## Evidence

- Regression on unchanged production code: the manual-install and copied-journal cases fail with CLI exit 1 through `reportUpdateCommandPendingRecovery`. With the fix, all seven cases in the publication-admission table pass, including verified installed-candidate recovery and refusal while a published launcher remains installed.
- Node-floor integration: npm/Node 26.4.0 rejects before staging or state database creation; four runtime-floor cases pass.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`, touched-file oxlint and oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and madge pass (0 import cycles).
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main`: passes, 1,280 lines of slack. Production +84/-25 (net +59); tests +76/-21 (net +55); docs +13/-3. New cases reuse the existing fixture and table; no useful coverage was removed to offset them.
- Codex autoreview of the complete local diff against `2e628e80c294d67e4fd903cbe2334fcc0aa28758`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The final review included complete journal, settlement, custody, and activation owner context; the reviewer did not execute tests.
- Full `check:changed` was omitted because of the known SQLite-inventory stall on this host. PR CI remains broad proof.

Live CLI proof used synthetic npm tarballs installed with `npm install --global --prefix <fixture> --ignore-scripts`, isolated HOME/state/temp directories, and the current source CLI. A real publication journal was left at `publication-complete`, an external npm install replaced its candidate and launcher, and the control directory was copied to change its identities. `openclaw update --dry-run --json --tag 2026.10.8` reported that recovery admission could proceed. `openclaw update repair --json --yes` exited 0 with the stale-journal warning and archived the operation. Independent checks confirmed identical current package bytes/launcher, the unchanged original descriptor, and retained recovery trees. The next update passed package recovery and reached the separate schema-downgrade guard (current-source fixture state 35 versus released target 20). This proves CLI recovery admission and settlement, not a complete published-package upgrade. The synthetic package also produced a plugin-readiness JSON warning during repair; repair kept exit 0 and did not restart a service.

All 50 test files selected by `rg -l 'package-update-activation(-journal)?' --glob '*.test.ts' src extensions packages test` were exercised. After correcting the settlement-reason assertion and updating the obsolete-rollback contract, both affected CLI files pass: **37 tests**, 73.72 s wall time (51% tests, 46% compiler preparation). Across consumer coverage: 677 pass, 61 skip, and three inherited failures remain.

The three macOS `package-update-publication-ownership.test.ts` failures (`commit`, `rollback`, `foreign`) reproduce identically on the unchanged base: the preparation callback expects symlink GID 12 but receives the updater GID 20. The failure occurs before activation in the existing launcher ownership-normalization path. The same filtered base run fails 3 cases and passes 1 (31.53 s wall, 28.51 s file duration, 95% compiler preparation). No timeout, retry, baseline, or assertion was weakened to hide them. These are deterministic existing failures, not evidence of this journal repair.
